question: Should `tools.exec.denylist` override ordinary `tools.exec.mode: "full"`, legacy `security=full`/`ask=off`, per-session `/exec full`, and durable trust while preserving elevated full as the explicit break-glass bypass?
rationale: Current main defines several no-prompt and break-glass paths, while this PR introduces a stricter operator-authored policy whose exact precedence changes a security and compatibility contract; code review cannot safely choose that product boundary.

options.title: Adopt STOP rules with explicit break-glass
options.body: Make denylist rules override normal full/off and `/exec` policy, while elevated full remains the clearly documented intentional bypass.

options.title: Make STOP rules absolute
options.body: Require denylist approval even under elevated full, accepting a stronger but more disruptive change to the existing break-glass contract.

options.title: Decline the new policy surface
options.body: Retain the current allowlist/full model and close this PR and the linked feature direction.

recommendation.title: Adopt STOP rules with explicit break-glass
recommendation.body: Make denylist rules override normal full/off and `/exec` policy, while elevated full remains the clearly documented intentional bypass.

likelyOwner.reason: Repository history shows primary ownership of YOLO, full/off, approval lifecycle, and related exec-policy decisions.
